findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed duct tape on 2 areas of the grill cooler. The person in charge (PIC) stated it’s purpose was to cover switches. Discussed replacing the duct tape (which contains an adhesive that can degrade) with plastic or sheet metal. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. Correct by next routine inspectino.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the handle of a sugar scoop and cashew scoop in contact with ready to eat (RTE) foods. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) brought scoops to the dish area for ware washing. Ensure all RTE foods are protected from bare hand contamination by storing the handles above the foods, or separate from the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed tiles on the left side of the mop sink are coming loose. Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair. Ensure the tiles are re-adhered by the next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed multiple food contact surfaces to contain soil accumulation or food debris.
1) A slight amount of soil was observed on the ice machine. CORRECTED- the person in charge immediately wiped the soil area with a clean sanitizer wipe.
2) The ice outlets at the self service station in the lobby contained a slight amount of soil accumulation. CORRECTED- employee wiped the food contact surfaces with a clean sanitizer wipe.
3) A slight amount of food debris was observed on a spatula hanging in a ready-to-use position in the kitchen prep area. CORRECTED- the spatula was taken to the dish washing station to be cleaned and sanitized.
Ensure are food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed a soil accumulation along the perimeter of the walk-in cooler door. PARTIALLY CORRECTED- employee wiped the gaskets clean with a sanitizer solution. A small amount of soil debris was still present on the wall sealant on the side of the door hinge. A replacement sealant is recommended by the next routine inspection.
Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil or debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed some physical facilities in need or replacement or repair:
1) A tile on the left side of the mop sink is coming loose.
2) Multiple tiles underneath the dry storage (to the left of the walk-in cooler) were observed to be broken. Broken tiles pose a risk of cross-contamination and improper cleaning. 
3) A hole was observed in the wall underneath the dish machine (by PVC plumbing to sink).
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: One sanitizer bucket was observed with no measurable quat sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- PIC remade the sanitizer bucket, which was then observed at 200ppm quat. Ensure sanitizer buckets are remade regularly throughout the day to maintain their efficacy.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
A food employee was observed leaving the restroom and immediately beginning to don gloves. CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the employee and discussed the need to wash hands upon returning to work after using the restroom. The employee discarded the gloves, washed hands, then donned new gloves. Review when to wash hands with all employees.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Two of the ice cream scoop dipping wells do not have sufficient flow of running water to carry away food particles. The water spouts were observed not pouring into the dipping well containers. 
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (D) In running water with sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, if used with moist FOOD such as ice cream or mashed potatoes. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) 1st REPEAT: Broken and damaged floor tiles were observed in the walk-in cooler near the entrance to the walk-in freezer. Repair or replace broken tiles so that the floor is smooth and easily cleanable, and water does not collect where tiles are missing. 
2) 2nd REPEAT: Significant gap observed between the trim tiles and the wall under the dish machine and its drainboards. Repair so that wall and floor are sealed together. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Two outlet covers behind the shake station are cracked and missing portions. Replace the damaged outlet covers.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Two sanitizer buckets were observed with low or no measurable quat concentration. CORRECTED- Buckets were emptied and remade from the wall-mounted dispenser. Fresh sanitizer was observed at 200ppm quat. Discussed sanitizer remake timing. Ensure sanitizer buckets are maintained at an effective concentration (200-400ppm quat). 
4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
An open gallon of milk was observed in the shake prep cooler with a manufacturer use-by date of 1/27/24. CORRECTED- Milk was voluntarily discarded. Monitor foods to ensure they are used or discarded within 7 days of opening, not exceeding the manufacturer printed use-by dates.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Soil and debris accumulation observed under shelving in the walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer and along the floor/wall junction in dry storage, walk-in cooler, and walk-in freezer. Clean under shelving.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) 1st REPEAT: One floor tile near the dish machine is missing and several others are broken. Repair or replace so that floor is smooth and easily cleanable, and water does not collect where tiles are missing.
2) 1st REPEAT: Significant gap observed between the trim tiles and the wall under the dish machine and its drainboards. Repair so that wall and floor are sealed together. 
3) Broken and damaged floor tiles were observed in the walk-in cooler near the entrance to the walk-in freezer. Repair or replace broken tiles so that the floor is smooth and easily cleanable, and water does not collect where tiles are missing.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Soil and debris accumulation observed under shelving in the walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer and along the floor/wall junction in dry storage, walk-in cooler, and walk-in freezer. Clean physical facilities as often as necessary to keep them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) One floor tile near the dish machine is missing and several others are broken. Repair or replace so that floor is smooth and easily cleanable, and water does not collect where tiles are missing.
2) Significant gap observed between the trim tiles and the wall under the dish machine and its drainboards. Repair so that wall and floor are sealed together. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Weather stripping on the lower left side of the back door appears to be getting worn. Daylight is visible through the gap when the door is closed. Replace weather stripping to ensure door is tight fitting and protects against entry of pests.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee working in dining area was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. PIC coached employee on proper technique and noted the employee was aware of best practices and would ensure proper handwashing moving forward.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Covered portions of cooked, cooling pot roast were observed in two pans stacked together in the walk-in cooler. Condensation was present on inner surface of lids, and internal temperatures were observed at 46F (top pan) and 47F (bottom pan). Time stamp of 10:38 was observed on labels. PIC discussed process for cooking, cooling (on ice bath), and portioning of product. Exact time when cooling began was not certain, but based on the time stamp it was assumed the pot roast was in the last few hours of the cooling process. Lids were removed and portions were placed on a cart in the walk-in freezer to quickly finish chilling to 41F/below.
When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Wiping cloths were not properly submerged in sanitizer solution in sani-bucket at the cook line. Wiping cloths in top were stacked above the solution sticking out of the bucket. Proper storage of wiping cloths between uses was discussed with staff working in the area at the time of inspection. Extra wiping cloth was removed from sani-bucket to allow for proper storage of remaining cloths.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-buckets was observed 100ppm and below. GM noted solutions were just checked within the 20 minutes prior to inspectors arrival. Procedure for setup of sani-buckets includes soaking wiping cloths in a separate quat solution prior to placing wiping cloths in sani-buckets for use. Fresh solutions were provided and observed at 200ppm. See general comments for additional information.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Washing fruits and vegetables
findings.citation_text:
3-302.15 Food employee was observed slicing lemons that were stored in the original cardboard box. Employee stated lemons were cleaned the previous day and placed back in the box because a clean storage tub was not available at the time. Lemons were re-washed prior to continuing with prep, and proper storage of washed produce was discussed. The original boxes are not considered a clean surface, and washed lemons should be stored in food grade liner bags in the future if re-use of the box is required for some reason.  
Raw fruits and vegetables shall be thoroughly washed in water to remove soil and other contaminants before being cut, combined with other ingredients, cooked, served, or offered for human consumption in ready-to-eat form.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook line employee was observed going between glove changes without handwashing in between. Employee was educated on handwashing between glove changes. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed between glove changes and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee working at grill was observed adjusting clothing with gloved hands and continued to food handling without a handwash and glove change. Employee was educated on proper glove use prior to washing hands and putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with prep. Employee was observed changing gloves and washing hands as needed for remainder of inspection.
-Employee working at drive thru window was observed wearing gloves and then put on another pair of single use gloves on top to prepare a beverage order. Glove use policy was discussed with management, and double gloving is not in the policy. Employee was educated by manager on duty.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-buckets was at 0ppm at the front counter and 100ppm by ice cream station. Solutions were changed and observed at 200ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. 

Dish machine final rinse concentration was at 0ppm chlorine. Sanitizer bucket was approximately a quarter full of product, and PIC noted the amount of sanitizer in the chemical bucket was potentially too low to allow for proper suction. Changing to a full bucket and priming the dish machine sanitizer line resulted in a final rinse concentration of 100ppm.
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket located by the ice cream machine and the sanitizer bucket located by the drive thru drink station were tested and found to have a concentration of 0ppm QUAT sanitizer solution. These solutions were brought to management’s attention and were immediately removed from service and replaced with fresh sanitizer solutions. The fresh solutions were both tested and observed at 100ppm QUAT sanitizer. Ensure that the sanitizer buckets are tested a frequency to allow the solution to be changed when necessary to allow the sanitizer solution to perform its function.
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The following areas were observed to need replacement caulking: The hand sink by the ice cream area and the mop sink where it is connected to the floor. Ensure these surfaces are repaired by removing any old caulking and replacing it with a fresh seal that creates a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The floor tiles by the mop sink basin are observed to be damaged. Ensure these tiles are removed and replaced with new tiles that creates a repaired surface that creates a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable seal with the mop sink basin.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed going between handling soiled and clean dishes without a hand wash in between. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. GM had employee wash his hands, and clean equipment previously handled was placed through another ware washing cycle.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed between handling soiled and clean equipment and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee at front counter service area was observed adjusting his jacket sleeves with gloved hands. GM spoke to employee about proper use of gloves. Gloves were discarded.
--Cook retrieved food from the 4 door freezer to drop food in the fryer and then handled a bun for sandwich preparation without a glove change in between. Proper glove use was discussed. GM advised cook about glove changes after touching general surfaces, and cook was observed changing gloves as needed for the remainder of inspection. 
NOTE: Best practice requires glove changes after touching general surfaces that are not considered clean, including but not limited to, handles of cold holding equipment and clothing.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-603.12 Utensil in clean storage drawer was observed with what appeared to be stuck on food debris or possibly rust on the food contact surface. GM placed utensil in dish area to go through ware washing. If rust rather than food debris is present, discard the utensil. Otherwise, staff should be advised on precleaning and repeating the steps of ware washing as many times as necessary to ensure removal of soil from all surfaces
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee in back prep area did not wash hands upon exiting the walkin cooler and prior to putting on gloves to continue with prep. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks and prior to putting on gloves. Employee was observed washing hands between tasks as needed for the remainder of the inspection
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handsink at front service/drive thru area had ice in the basin indicating use as a dump sink. Staff and management were advised to cease the practice of using the handsink for anything other than handwashing.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-buckets was at 0ppm at the front counter and ice cream station. Manager noted the solutions were prepared recently. Fresh solution was dispensed in a bucket and observed at 200ppm. Manager was advised some wiping cloths when dry and placed in fresh sanitizer solution absorb chemical out of the solution. Ensure the wiping cloths are rinsed with sanitizer from the dispenser prior to placing in fresh solution to maintain concentration. Use test strips to verify concentration. Check solutions during operations and change as needed. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. 

Dish machine final rinse concentration was at 0ppm chlorine. Proper suction was not occurring because the tube as pushed down to far and curled up in the bottom of the chemical bucket. Manager adjusted the tubing, provided a fresh/full chemical bucket, and primed the sanitizer line. After two full cycles the dish machine final rinse concentration was observed at 100ppm. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Stem of food thermometer available for use on the cook line was soiled with grease and food crumbs. Thermometer was cleaned and calibrated during inspection. Ensure the stems of food thermometers are wiped between uses with sanitizer and properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use.
Food contact surfaces of food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storing and sanitized before use after cleaning. 

Underneath surface of heat lamp at fry station hot holding was soiled with accumulation of stuck on grease. Debris as hanging over where fried foods are held prior to service.
Clean the underside of the heat lamp as needed to eliminate buildup that could fall onto food. 

Baffle inside ice machine was soiled with mold accumulation, especially along the lower edge. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness
findings.citation_text:
2-402.11 Female employee with long blonde hair was walking around in the kitchen and front service area without hair restraint. Manger on duty noted she was in the process of setting up equipment. Staff were advised that at minimum long hair needs to be pulled back in a ponytail while working in the kitchen around food and equipment regardless of the task being performed. Employee pulled hair back in a ponytail, and all staff were observed with hair properly restrained upon opening for business.
Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, hair coverings or nets, beard restraints, and clothing that covers body hair, that are designed and worn to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; and unwrapped single service and single use articles.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee that opened the back door with gloved hands to allow inspector access for inspection was observed returning to dish area and continuing to work without changing gloves. Employee was approaching clean dishes and was advised to ensure gloves are changed after touching general surfaces such as the back door. Employee discarded gloved in question.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) dish machine - top/general surfaces (buildup);
B) fryers - surfaces between and underneath (grease/food debris); and
C) heat lamp at fry station hot holding - general surfaces (grease).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen awareness training was not available for CFMs. Manager on duty contacted GM during inspection. The internal eLearning program may qualify. GM was going to check with corporate on this matter as of the previous routine inspection. An ANSI/ASTM accredited allergen awareness training certification is required for certified food managers at high risk facilities, and certifications needs to be maintained on-site along with manager certifications. 
Provide copies of allergen training certifications for CFMs by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener was observed to have buildup on the blade. Can opener was placed in the dish area to go through ware washing.
Slicer used for tomatoes was observed in storage area and had food debris stuck on the cutting surface. Slicer was taken to dish area to go through ware washing process. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours. If debris remains after the ware washing cycle is complete, then repeat the process to ensure all food and general debris is removed prior to storing equipment for later use.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Grilled onions in the hot holding well by the grill were observed with surface and internal temperatures at 120-130F. Mushrooms in the same hot holding unit were at 135F. Onions were just prepared within the 30 minutes prior. An insert in the bottom of the pan was likely the reason the onions were not maintaining temperature. Onions were placed back on the grill and reheated to 167F. The insert was removed so onions were in direct contact with the pan to allow for hotter holding temperature.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 A portion of fish in the top of a container at breading station had internal temperature of 46F. Portion above 45F was discarded. Other fish lower in the pan were observed at 40F-45F. 
Mint and chocolate custard mix were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 47F-48F in the hoppers. Vanilla custard mix was observed at 39F. GM emptied the remainder of mint and chocolate custard mixes to clean and sanitize the hoppers prior to putting in fresh product. New product was observed at 38F. GM discovered the remaining portions were likely above 41F due to a senor in the hopper but will check into the matter further for troubleshooting in order to avoid issues in the future. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:
5-103.12 Cold water was not available at the front counter/drive thru handsink. GM stated it was working earlier in the day and attempted repairs to the components of the faucet. Repairs have been made to the faucet for this issue in the past. The cold water worked temporarily but was later not working again. GM called for service; plumber will be out tomorrow to assess repairs. Replacement parts can no longer be ordered for the sink in question, and a new faucet will have to be installed. Hot water was available at the sink to allow for handwashing, and another handwashing sink was available around the corner.
Water under pressure must be provided to all fixtures and equipment requiring water connections to operate.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Dust accumulation was observed on the air exchange vent cover adjacent to the walkin cooler. Clean the air exchange vent cover.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Food debris was observed on slicer used to cut tomatoes during morning prep. Equipment was hanging in the designated clean storage area. Slicer was placed in dirty dish area for cleaning. Manager noted the slicer was rinsed prior to running through the dish machine earlier but would be cleaned and sanitized again.
 
Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) lemon slicer (stuck on food debris);   and
B) ceiling inside ice machine behind baffle (mold).
Manager noted lemon slicer was not used for a couple days, and was placed in the dirty dish area to go through ware washing process again. 
Cleaning and maintenance of the ice machine were discussed. Ice machine was just cleaned less than a month ago. Consider detail cleaning inside where mold growth was observed more frequently.

To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use (slicers, knives, cutting boards, etc.) or at a frequency that will eliminate buildup of mold/debris (ice machine, etc.).

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floor between the wall and concrete machine was soiled with buildup single service articles and food debris. Clean the floor in the aforementioned area.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Dust accumulation was observed on the wall above the microwave on the cook line and on the air exchange vent cover adjacent to the walkin cooler. Clean the walls in the aforementioned areas.

Walls and attached equipment shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Two employees at different times were observed washing their hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Handwashing technique was discussed with both employees. GM was advised to reiterate proper handwashing technique with all staff.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Dry hands with paper towels prior to using paper towels as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket on the cook line was observed with a concentration at ~100ppm; the solution was murky and ready to be changed. All other solutions were remade around the time inspector arrived, but the cook line solution was missed. Solution was changed by GM.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Mold accumulation was observed on the surfaces of ice shoots of the dining area soda machine. Cleaning and sanitizing of ice shoots was discussed with GM.

Clean and sanitize ice shoots daily to eliminate buildup of mold, and maintain ice shoots clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Chicken breasts in the grill cold holding rail had surface and internal temperatures at 51°F and 52°F respectively. Chicken was in the cold holding unit since start of business for the day. Chicken breasts were discarded and replaced with fresh product. Also, reuben portions in the cold rail had an internal temperature of 48°F on the top layer and a surface temperature of 43°F further down inside the pan. Cold rail was frosted, and the bottom holding area was observed at 40°F. Lid up top was closed to help maintain colder temperature. Manager was advised to monitor the temperatures of meats in the cold rail and rotate/discard product accordingly.

Vanilla and chocolate custard in the hopper had internal temperatures at 46°F-49°F and 50°F-52°F. Manager on duty contacted store manager at the request of inspector. Upon troubleshooting via phone with the store manager, the manager on duty discovered the hopper was turned off. Store manager advised the manager on duty to waste the remaining product in the hopper. Hopper would be cleaned and sanitized prior to placing new product inside.

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - Sundae cup was observed stored inside almond slices in the dry storage area. Sundae cup was removed and discarded. 

To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees; use scoops with handles for dispensing ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.160 & 510 - Cook was observed going between working with raw meat at the grill and then handling ready to eat foods without washing hands and changing gloves. Handwashing and glove use were discussed with the cook and manager on duty. Cook washed his hands and put on a new pair of gloves prior to continuing with food prep.

Gloves are intended for one task and shall be changed when they become torn, soiled, or there is an interruption in task. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
NOTE: Always wash hands and change gloves when switching from raw to ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat test kit was not available for checking the concentration of solution in sani-buckets. Obtain and use quat test strips to check the concentration of sanitizer dispensed at the 3 part sink.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.
NOTE: Chlorine test kits were available for checking the dish machine sanitizer.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-buckets at front counter and by concrete mixing station were at 0-100ppm quat. An employee stated they were more than likely prepared earlier that morning. Solutions were remade and observed at proper concentration (200ppm).

Change sanitizer in buckets every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently if wiping cloths and solutions become heavily soiled. Let the chemical run through the line for several seconds before filling buckets, and soak wiping cloths in sanitizer prior to placing in fresh sanitizer solution (dry wiping cloths sometimes absorb chemical).
Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) walkin cooler shelves (splash/mold - around fish storage);   and
B) scale in prep area (food splash/buildup).

Clean general surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Utensil storage drawers in back prep area were observed with accumulation of splash and food crumbs. Clean and sanitize the utensil storage drawers as needed, and maintain them clean.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Plastic spoons were observed with food surfaces extended up out of storage container by the drive thru window. Manager arranged all spoons to allow for proper storage with handles presented up.

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - None of the employees working at the time of inspection had a current food manager certification. Manager on duty stated he just took the food sanitation course ~2wks ago at St. John's and is awaiting his results. Manager was advised that proof of his certification needs to be provided prior to the scheduled follow-up date to avoid a re-inspection (See general comments).

Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  licensed certified food managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of certified food managers.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) ice shoots of dining area soda machine (mold);   and
B) inner surface of ice machine lid (dust).
Clean and sanitize the aforementioned food contact surfaces regularly to eliminate buildup of mold and dust.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Top cold holding rail of the cooler at the far end of the cookline was not turned on prior to placing foods inside. Burger patty and corned beef in the cookline cooler were 54F-55F, while chicken patties in the unit were at 41F-43F. Manager turned on the cold holding rail and noted the products in question were stocked in the cooler less than an hour prior. All products were moved to the walkin cooler until the cold rail reached temperature to allow for proper cold holding. Cold holding unit at the front counter used for sour cream packets, butter, and dressings was observed to be off (+60F) and stocked with product. Manager turned on the unit and switched out products.
 
Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - A) Fry salt and grill seasoning scoops were observed to be soiled in storage containers on top of bulk storage bins. Clean and sanitize scoops and storage containers at minimum at the end of operations daily.

Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

B) Plastic cup was observed inside bulk nut container in the dry storage area. Obtain and use a proper scoop with a handle.

Use suitable utensils for dispensing foods (e.g. scoops with handles) to avoid unnecessary manual contact with food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 1160 - Employee doing tomato prep put on gloves without first washing her hands and then proceeded to adjust the sleeves of her fleece jacket. Inspector spoke with employee on handwashing and proper use of gloves. Employee washed her hands prior to putting on a new pair of gloves and continuing with prep.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Upon arrival inspector observed three sani-buckets to be at 0-100ppm quat respectively. Solutions were prepared recently. Freshly dispensed solution was observed at 200ppm with facility and inspector's test strips. Towels used in sani-buckets absorb sanitizer and need to be soaked in quat solution prior to adding towels to the sani-buckets. Solutions were re-made and observed at 200ppm

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) ice shoots of the dining area soda machine (mold);  and
B) coffee maker under grounds basket (buildup). 

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - A) Single service knives were observed with food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. Store utensils all facing the same direction, with handles presented out, so food contact surfaces are not touched when utensils are retrieved.

B) Custard cup caddy by drive thru was soiled with general buildup in the bottom. Clean the caddy and needed, and maintain it clean.

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Cheese slices in the top holding area of the prep cooler had surface temperatures above 41F. One piece of Swiss cheese was observed at 48F and was immediately discarded. Cheddar and Havarti slices had internal temperatures of 53F and 54F respectively. Cook noted they were placed in the cooler around 2p. Staff were advised to use or discard the cheese slices by 6p. All other foods had surface and internal temperatures at 43F and 40F.
Keep the lid closed as much as possible to help maintain colder temperatures in the top holding area of the cook line prep cooler.

All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41F/below while on display and service.
NOTE: If it difficult to maintain foods at 41F/below in the top holding area of the prep cooler, consider establishing a time control policy (use/discard w/in 4hrs).

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.160 - Employee left the cook line and handled a personal beverage with gloved hands. The employee then proceeded to the storage area to retrieve a package of to go containers and was observed preparing to stock containers without changing gloves. Employee washed hands and put on a new pair of gloves to complete the task.
Employees were also observed touching various surfaces (handles of freezer, buttons of equipment, and edge of garbage can) with gloved hands while working on the cook line and continuing on to the next task without changing gloves. Staff on cook line were advised on proper glove use and all staff washed hands and put on a new pair of gloves before continuing with food preparation.

Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - A partially eaten frozen custard treat was observed in the walkin freezer. Manager discarded the custard in the trash.

Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - Edges of cabinets used for storage of garbage cans on both sides of the condiment/beverage self service area were damaged along the inner edges. Rough, unsealed particle board was present. Provide repairs to the edges of the garbage can cabinets. The end result needs to be smooth, easily cleanable and able to be maintained in a sanitary condition.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sani-buckets all tested at 0ppm quat. A fresh sanitizer solution was obtained from the dispenser and observed at 0ppm. The chemical bottle was less than 1/4 full, and the chemical was not pulling through the dispensing tube. Manager added chemical to the jug, and all buckets were remade. Concentration was observed at 200ppm when chemical jug was refilled.
Train all staff on proper use of the sanitizer dispensing system and how to use the quat test strips to verify the sanitizer solutions are at proper concentration (200ppm).

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 .& 1220 - A) Front edge of mopsink was worn where caulk was used for repairs. Re-seal the floor around the front edge of the mopsink.

B) Baseboard was missing at the floor to wall juncture at the corner under the 3 part sink. Exposed wood beams and insulation were observed. Staff noted it was due to some issues with the dish machine and adjustments that were made. Make proper repairs at the floor to wall juncture at the corner under the 3 part sink.

C) Damaged, loose piece of ceramic baseboard was observed on the left side of the back door. Repair or replace the piece of ceramic baseboard.

D) Floors were soiled in the following areas:
1. under in-use soda syrup in dry storage (plastic caps/general buildup);  and
2. walkin freezer - under shelving (food debris/splash).
Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250 Observed the left side of the preparation cooler to be holding foods at temperatures in the mid-50s. The upper left side holds a number of items that are not considered potentially hazardous (PH). Probed PH foods include: 1) cheese shreds (probed at 54F - nearly empty after lunch rush) and 2) 1000 Island dressing (probed 53F). The lid of the preparation cooler is observed opened even though the lunch rush had subsided. The lids of the unit were closed during the inspection. Temperature logs for the facility are maintained at least three times daily at this unit. The manager is advised to monitor the left and right side of this cooler. Air movement through the top of the unit may be effected in multiple ways resulting in one half of the cooler being warmer than the other. Monitoring the top two sides of this cooler will allow management to recognize if a mechanical failure is occurring.  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-160b Observed a gloved employee switch tasks from food handling to cell phone handing and begin to return to food handling without properly washing hands and changing gloves. Gloves are intended to protect the food from the employee. Discussed glove use with employee and manager. See that staff understand when to wash hands and change gloves. Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b The sani-bucket on the dessert line (shake mixer) is observed loaded with cloths and testing at 0pp quat residual. Monitor sani-buckets and see that they are changed on a sufficiently frequent basis to maintain solution at 200ppm Quat residual. Various activities will impact the concentration in solution. Changing buckets after heavy use (fats, grease, and gross food materials will reduce chemical concentration) or keeping too many towels from being stored within the bucket will help maintain solution at proper concentration. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1330 An opened spray bottle of degreaser is observed on the top shelf of the cookline (adjacent to the microwave and over a hot holding unit). Bottle was moved to the floor during the inspection. Store chemicals in such a manner as to prevent the potential cross-contamination due to spills. Personal medications shall not be stored in food storage, preparation, or service areas. Properly store personal medications.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750-1300 Observed an unlabeled spray bottle to be stored on the sprayer nozzle of the triple sink on the backline. Labeled during the inspection. Properly label all chemicals and clear liquids.  Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140b  The wet batter at the fish batter station is probed at 48F. The batter was recently made (within the half hour or hour). Fish in this cold held station is observed at 39-40F. Ice was added to the batter during the inspection. The temperature of the batter dropped to 40F. Watch that foods are rapidly cooled for cold holding or indicate the time the food was created on the container.   All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.  Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 The edges of the shelves holding the two garbage cans in the lobby self-service area are observed to be peeling. Maintain these surfaces smooth and easily cleanable.  Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b The sanitizer dispenser broke just prior to the inspection. The manager had attempted to hand add chemical to the buckets. Buckets tested at 0ppm Quat. More chemical was added during the inspection. Fresh buckets tested at 200ppm Quat during the inspection. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 The floor drain beneath the custard machine is observed soiled with mold and food debris. Clean the floor drain.  Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750- 1220: The cabinet beneath the soda station at the drive thru is observed rusted, soiled, and with minimal standing water. Clean and maintain this cabinet shelving. Manager stated he would work on the cabinet today. Also, the counter beneath the lobby soda machine is observed soiled with syrup and single-service debris (look towards the back of the counter). Wall, ceilings, and attached equipment shall be maintained in good repair. Clean and maintain counters and shelving.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-120: Several foods on top of the preparation cooler were probed. The majority of the foods are observed between the temperatures of 38-40F. Portion cups of cheese shreds are observed at 70-73F. These cups were observed flowing over the top of a deep container/over the chill line of the cooler. They were overstocked after the lunch hour. Cheese cups were moved to the lower base of the prep cooler - this portion was holding temperature at 38F. Also, a single sauce (shallow pan) in the right side of the prep cooler is holding temperature at 53F. The remaining items in the cooler were at proper temperature. The shallow amount of sauce will be used within four hours. Cease stocking product over the fill lines of coolers and containers.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Sani-solution tested within the four buckets located around the kitchen indicated just under 100ppm in solution. The  wall mounted dispenser is properly dispensing product at 200ppm Quat. There are a number of towels being held within each bucket. During the inspection, fresh solution was added to all buckets. Either the cloths should be dipping in solution prior to being added to the bucket OR the solution was not at proper concentration as it was filled for the morning. MAKE SURE THE BUCKETS ARE CHECKED.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed the bottom of portion cups of cheese shreds being stored in the same container as bulk cheese shreds. Avoid allowing the bottom of a container to be in direct contact with food. Portion cups were removed during the inspection. Discussed with manager that the potential for cross-contamination from the bottom of the portion cup to the food. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the cabinet of the drive-thru soda compressor and the frontline cooler holding butter to be soiled. The drive thru soda cabinet has spilled soda around the compressor and the filter of the lift-lid frontline cooler is dusty. Clean these two areas. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 The coving to the left of back door is broken. Replace/repair the broken section of coving. Also, to the left of the 3-part sink, the coving is not properly sealed to the wall. Seal the top of the tile to the wall. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-280 A cup is observed being used as a scoop in the bulk salt and pepper holder in the dry storage room. Pulled from service during the inspection. To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees or provided to consumers who serve themselves. 750-280 the no-salt fry scoop was observed being stored within an uncleanable portion of the overhead fry lamp. Stored on the cleanable  flat top of the light during the inspection.  Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The back of the soda station by the drive-thru was soiled with accumulated syrup where the  two pieces of stainless steel meet. Cleaned during the inspection. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 REPEAT: Lobby cabinets (especially under the soda machine and shelves holding garbages) are observed to have flaking and chipping edges. See notes in General Comments - repairs will occur within the next several weeks. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 An unprotected sleeve of cups was observed stored within the cabinet housing the soda compressor for the drive-thru soda machine. The base of this cabinet is dusty and rusty from the activity of the compressor. Cups were discarded during the inspection. Manager stated policy is that nothing be stored within these cabinets. Policy is consistent with what is observed throughout facility. Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250: The open air dressing cooler on the frontline is observed to be holding dressings at 45-49F. A ranch dressing portion cup was probed = 45F. A stem thermometer left in the cooler indicated 49F. The cooler base is holding temperature at 34F. Quantity in open air unit was halved and portions placed within base cooler. Discussed possible equipment additions to help with temperature control. Also, use of time as control with use of stem thermometer.   All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 The lobby cabinets have a few edges that are starting to peel and reveal the particle board beneath. The interior cabinet edges of the garbage bins, the cabinet holding the soda station drain lines, and the other garbage cabinet have peeling laminate. Seal the counters so edges are smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable. Do not allow cabinets to mold and become a breeding ground for pests.  Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750-830f REPEAT: There continue to be observed multiple lids and containers with old labels attached. Observed 'use first' labels, orange rectangle date marking stickers, and strips of masking tape on various lids in various states of peeling and removal. Get the stickers off during the washing process. Old adhesive collects food debris and soil. Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment: 750-1240 The light bulb over the walk-in freezer door is not shielded and does not appear to be shatterproof. Most of the bulbs in the facility are shatterproof and the manager was able to produce shatterproof bulbs used within the facility, however, the WIF bulb does not feel shatterproof. Provide a light shield for the bulb. All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed cardboard being used as a divider between single-service bbq and ranch dressings on the fronrtline - beneath the cash register. During the inspection, manager was able to cut a thin piece of plastic to use as a divider and discard the cardboard. ALSO, the edges of the shelving in the cube cooler beneath the toppings station has edges that are beginning to peel. Reseal the shelving so peeling paint doesn't fall into food product stored within cooler. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750-830f Throughout facility observed various masking tape and small white sticker labels still adhered to blue plastic lids and metal lids. Make sure that labels are removed as part of the dish washing process. Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The cabinet beneath the ice bin of the drive-thru soda station is observed to have some soil, ponding water, and an old fruit fly soiled information packet. Item was discarded during inspection, clean the base shelf of this cabinet. ALSO, the top shelf of the plastics storage in the back is dusty. Clean the top shelf storing large plastic tubs and remove dust from the surface. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: Rolling cart parked in front of hand sink near meat cooler and employee restroom. 750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times. Do not block area in front of hand sink. Cart was removed.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: No test kit is available for the quat sanitizer. 750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. Provide a test kit for the quat sanitizer. Quat sanitizer shall be 200ppm and chlorine in the dish shall be 50 ppm.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Wet wiping cloths are observed to be sitting on the top of the custard machine and the table at shake making. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: The caulk lines at the prep area and dish areas have some soil in the line area. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings. Remove caulk seal, clean and re-seal these areas with fresh caulk.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleansable. There is a practice of having towels under pans and around food prep area. Towels if used for wiping shall be stored in sanitizer between uses. These towels make the non food surfaces absorbent and not easily cleansable. Discontinue using towels in this manner.
